name: Old Mission Peninsula

climate.koppen_name: Cold, no dry season, warm summer

climate: Seasons this cool ripen Pinot Gris, Riesling, Pinot Noir, Müller-Thurgau and Gewürztraminer fully without cooking off their freshness.
Riesling, Pinot Noir and Pinot Gris sit in their sweet spot, so the wines can show the style they are known for.
Chardonnay is at its cool limit. In cool years it can stay underripe, with green, sharp flavors.
Rain picks up at harvest. Growers race to pick before rot sets in, and vintages vary more.

soil.rock: Shale and mudstone are fine-grained rocks that hold heat well and are moderately fertile. Limestone makes alkaline soil that drains well yet can hold water for the vines. It is usually planted to grapes valued for their acidity.
soil.top: The topsoil drains fast and warms early in spring. Vines get little water, which keeps crops small and flavors concentrated, but drought bites hard. Its pH is close to neutral, so vines take up the nutrients they need easily.

land: Gentle slopes. Enough tilt to drain cold air and rain away, which lowers frost risk, yet still easy to farm by machine.

winkler: Only very early grapes ripen well, mostly hybrids and a few vinifera.
